thread:
alejandro: quick heads-up — saw a 3.2s tail spike on mistral-7b when requests crossed the sliding-window -> max_pos boundary this morning. repro with streaming traffic.
maria: ugh, exact repro steps?
alejandro: sequence length pattern: normal seqs ~1024, then a long noisy input ~4500 that triggers wraparound. latency histogram shows a sharp tail only when we cross the model's max_position_embeddings window.
devon: can you paste the profiler snippet? thinking kernel selector might be falling back to the generic attention path on wrap.
alejandro: pasted below
```
profiles: {
  request_id: xq-44
  seq_len: 4500
  sliding_window: 512
  rope_scale: 1.0
  kernel_chosen: "attn_generic_fallback"
  kv_ops: "evict+remap"
  tokens_generated: 72
  tail_latency_ms: 3200
}
```
sarah: interesting — on M7B we usually pick the fused_matmul or tiled_attn kernels. Why did selector choose generic? maybe mask pattern after wrap is non-contiguous.
kai: could be the attention mask has a full-row masked block due to padding+wrap; our kernel cost model penalizes irregular masks and picks fallback.
maria: confirm: kernel selector decision path uses mask sparsity heuristics + estimated memory stride. If mask looks 'dense' but with holes we sometimes pick generic because tiling assumptions break.
alejandro: exact. I dumped the mask matrix around the boundary — there's a run of padded tokens then text, so the mask has a long diagonal shift. That apparently breaks our vectorized attention tile prefetch.
devon: any change in rope scaling? rope_scale adjustments sometimes push numeric ranges and change kernel numerics.
alejandro: rope_scale was default 1.0 for this run. I tried rope_scale 0.5 quickly and kernel stayed same, but latency improved ~400ms (weird). suspect cache alignment and KV layouts.
sarah: can you share the minimal repro command? I'll try to run on a local dev GPU cluster.
alejandro: sure
```
./bench.sh --model mistral-7b --seq 4600 --sliding-window 512 --batch 1 --rope-scale 1.0 --seed 42 --profile
```
kai: I'll instrument kernel selector logs to see the exact cost scores. If it's the mask heuristic we can tweak threshold for 'tiling_compatible' for sequences that wrap only once.
maria: there's also a KV cache eviction path we recently changed in 2.3.4: when maxpos wraps we remap offsets instead of shifting base pointer. If remap code introduces non-coalesced loads, fused kernels suffer.
devon: right — remap leads to strided accesses. Fused tiled kernels need contiguous KV tiles. Generic handles it but slower.
alejandro: profiling memory ops shows a bunch of 64B strided loads after remap.
